metadata.title: Europe wild camping: tents and open bivouacs
metadata.scope: European countries, microstates, Kosovo and transcontinental neighbours; dependencies and overseas territories are not systematically covered.
metadata.activity: Nonmotorized bikepacker or walker; short overnight tent or shelterless bivouac.
metadata.excluded_activity: Campervan, motorhome, caravan parking or sleeping; commercial campsite licensing except where it directly controls occasional tents.
metadata.status: Research overview, not a production geofence or an exhaustive municipal legal database.
method: National pass first; selected state, municipality, park and landowner exceptions second.
Prefer legislation, regulators, park authorities and landowners. Distinguish law from guidance and tolerance.
Search-result review is weaker than full-text review and is identified per source.
Lack of verified enforcement does not mean tolerance. Red denotes an explicit applicable prohibition, not a predicted probability of a fine.
Country colors summarize the regime; local green records do not grant permission outside their stated scope.
Natural Earth country and selected subnational polygons are cartographic overview fills. Local park and landowner markers are approximate orientation points, never legal-area polygons.
Sources are a dated snapshot; signs, closure notices and current local orders need rechecking.
Subagents independently checked northern and eastern regions. Conflicts between official visitor pages and statutes are recorded; the decree takes precedence where inspected.

Additional regional pass inspects Austrian states and alpine access, Swiss cantons/municipalities, German forest programmes, and Spanish/Italian local exceptions. Positive rights and expert interpretations are identified separately.
Community comments and travel articles identify leads. Verified official findings enter the rulebook; unsupported anecdotes and vehicle rules do not determine tent colours.
limitations: Local coverage is selective, strongest for popular bikepacking and mountain areas.
Exact municipal, forest-owner, reserve and program boundary datasets are not embedded.
Open sleeping, bivy bags, tarps, tents and emergency shelter can have distinct local definitions.
No inference that all national parks are forbidden or that every one-night stay is lawful.
Above-tree-line mode changes researched jurisdiction summaries. No forest, treeline, altitude, pasture or parcel boundary is inferred from a state outline.

product_assessment.worth_building: Useful as a sourced regional advisory plus links to permitted zones; unreliable as an unconditional GPS yes/no decision without authoritative boundary and freshness work.
decision_inputs: Tent versus open bivouac versus genuine emergency
Group size and number of nights
product_assessment.precedence: Apply all applicable layers. A higher-level permission can be restricted locally; a local permit can provide an explicit exception. A mere marker proximity must never override a country rule.
product_assessment.refresh: Review ordinary rules at least annually; permits, seasonal bans and closure notices before the trip.
issue_corrections: Do not mark every national park or reserve red. Several French, Finnish and other parks explicitly allow bivouacs.
Obwalden’s revoked implementing ordinance is not the current rule.
Korporation Uri policy applies to its land, not the whole canton; Göschenen and Seewlisee have exceptions.
A statutory maximum fine is not a likely or automatic fine.
Do not carry vehicle parking rules over to tent camping.
Muránska planina visitor pages conflict with the current decree about tent bivouacs. Use the decree’s shelterless emergency definition.
The historical Hungarian law URL ending .35 is not a current consolidation.
State forest pole-camping sites in the Netherlands closed permanently; old camping guides are stale.
Austrian alpine exceptions are state-specific; Upper Austria and Styria treat grazing differently.
Upper Austria expressly permits unpaid landholder-approved camping under §76(4); a campsite notification rule is not a blanket one-tent restriction.
Some local bivouac permissions include tents; others exclude tents or apply only to walking mountain traverses.
Polish overnight programme permissions can be withdrawn even when the same page retains an old positive description.

Picos de Europa visitor guidance retains an older 1600 m tent allowance. The inspected 2026 plan instead limits planned shelterless bivouac to qualifying mountain/climbing activity above 1800 m, with tents for adverse weather or force majeure.
Beskydy 18:00–09:00 tent permission applies to designated overnight sites, not the whole country.
Camping permission does not establish a right to cycle to a pitch; Coillte and Picos impose separate bicycle-access rules.

metadata.date_handling: Colors describe the sourced regime and its seasonal conditions. The overview does not automatically turn a seasonal prohibition off on today’s date.
metadata.tolerance_handling: Yellow is not inferred from lack of prosecutions. Explicit tolerance evidence and legal mode restrictions are separate fields.
metadata.data_use: Review status and source type are part of each claim. Low-confidence and historical evidence must not drive a production permission answer.
